title: [WT-04T] Tests: held-out acceptance cases for worktree provisioning at worker pre-flight
description:
WT-04's planner (architect-4ae016fb) split this row out of WT-04 (task-c20464ff64ca49fca4371dd9b5194364), whose six DoD items need twin wrapper code plus test cases for both harnesses. Together they come to about 500 net lines, over the 400-net review cap. This row writes the held-out acceptance tests. WT-04 implements the behaviour, hooks this suite into postflight.{sh,ps1}, and must pass it UNCHANGED. No new scope: these are the cases WT-04's DoD already requires. Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §1.1-§1.6, §6.5 and §7.2, and against the contract below. WT-04's plan follows the same contract word for word.

Objective: one held-out case list, shared by both wrappers, that pins down how a worker seat provisions its task worktree W or refuses to.

Deliverable:
1. New scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs, modelled on scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs:
   - Invocation: `node postflight-worktree.cjs <sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine>`. `<file> cli` is the fake CLI, which appends a line to <MOE_PROJECT_PATH>/.moe/wt-cli.log.
   - Each case gets a fresh repository under one mkdtemp root.
   - `MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=<case,...>` selects a subset, and `MOE_KEEP_WORKTREE_FIXTURE=1` keeps the root.
   - It runs every selected case and prints `[worktree] <case> ok` or `[worktree] <case> FAILED: <why>`. It exits 1 if any case failed. No output line may start with SKIP, because postflight-safe.mjs fails on that.
   - Fixture: `git init` with HEAD on refs/heads/main and core.autocrlf false. Tracked files: .gitignore containing `.worktrees/`, src/a.txt, .moe/project.json with settings {autoCommit:false}, and .moe/tasks/<task>.json. Commit them as the seed, then `git switch -c moe/control`.
   - A worktree-mode case hands the fake {mode:'worktree', path:<top>/.worktrees/<task>, branch:'moe/task/<task>', target:'main'}. <top> is the fixture's `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
2. scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js gets opt-in knobs only. With every knob unset, every answer stays byte-identical:
   - FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE (JSON) becomes the top-level `workspace` of the hasNext:true claim answer, as WT-01 returns it.
   - FAKE_CTX_WORKSPACE (JSON) becomes the top-level `workspace` of a get_context answer that has a taskId, as WT-02 returns it.
   - FAKE_CTX_COMMITS (a JSON array) becomes get_context task.commits.
   - report_blocked calls are logged with appendRpc() and answered {success:true,status:'BLOCKED'}.

Contract the cases pin. It applies to worker seats only:
- Mode comes from the fresh claim's top-level `workspace`, else from get_context's. If neither has one, the seat is in shared mode.
- Worktree mode runs these guards in order, all before any W work:
  1. git older than 2.38: MOE_WORKTREE_UNSUPPORTED_GIT. The line names the version git reported.
  2. Not a git work tree, or the project is not the git top level: MOE_WORKTREE_PROJECT_NOT_TOP.
  3. The control checkout's HEAD is not refs/heads/moe/control: MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING.
  4. The target is blank or refs/heads/<target> is missing: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
  5. A task.commits checkpoint or completion whose ref is neither moe/task/<task> nor the target (bare or refs/heads/ form), and whose sha is not an ancestor of refs/heads/<target>: MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH.
  6. On Windows only, len(W) + 1 + the longest tracked path in the target is over 240 and core.longpaths is not true: MOE_WORKTREE_PATH_TOO_LONG.
- W is <top>/.worktrees/<task> on moe/task/<task>.
  - A W that `worktree list --porcelain -z` shows (D:\x = /mnt/d/x) is reused, dirt included. A registered W with an empty index is first finished with the steps below.
  - If the branch exists but W is not registered, W is added with `worktree add --lock --reason "moe <task>" --no-checkout W moe/task/<task>`, without -b.
  - Otherwise it is added with `--no-track -b moe/task/<task> W refs/heads/<target>`.
  - In every case, `sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.moe/'` and `read-tree -mu HEAD` then run in W.
  - Success prints `[worktree] created|reused|re-added <W> on moe/task/<task>`, and the CLI launches as before.
- Any failed git step: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED. A W this session added, whose branch has no commits beyond the target, is unregistered and deleted. A directory that was already there is never touched.
- W/.moe exists, as a file, directory or link: MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT. Nothing is deleted.
- In shared mode, if refs/heads/moe/task/<task> exists and is not fully landed in HEAD: MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH. The test for fully landed: `merge-tree --write-tree HEAD moe/task/<task>` exits 0 and prints HEAD's tree.
- Every refusal prints `[ERROR] <CODE>: <detail>` and calls report_blocked once with {taskId, workerId, reason starting with the code}. It launches no CLI and exits 1.

NOT in scope:
- scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}: WT-04 implements the behaviour.
- Hooking the suite into postflight.{sh,ps1}: WT-04 does that once the suite is green, because a red suite there fails every seat's gate.
- CLI cwd and env: WT-05.
- Docs.

File note: task-01f37ac6 and task-c4e076cd (the CQ lane) also plan postflight-fake-proxy.js. Check that neither is assigned before editing it.

Verification: the suite exits 1 against today's wrappers on both engines, every case except shared-landed failing on an assertion. Then `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` exits 0.
definitionOfDone: scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs runs as `node postflight-worktree.cjs <sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine>`, with a `cli` fake-CLI mode and a MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY filter. It prints one `[worktree] <case> ok|FAILED` line per case, exits 1 if any case failed, and never prints a line starting with SKIP.

Provisioning cases assert the contract in the description. lifecycle (create, then reuse, re-add, moe-present): W registered, locked with reason `moe task-postflight`, on refs/heads/moe/task/task-postflight at main's tip; W/src/a.txt present and W/.moe absent; the control checkout's HEAD ref and sha, `ls-files -s` and status outside .moe all unchanged. On reuse, a marker in W's admin dir and W's dirt survive. On re-add, the branch tip is unchanged and its commit is checked out. resume: a get_context-only workspace is honoured. half-made: an empty-index W gets finished.

Guard cases git-old (a PATH git stub reporting 2.37.9; the log names it), not-top, control, target-missing, mismatch, dir-exists (the pre-existing directory is untouched), sparse-fail (the stub fails sparse-checkout; W ends up unregistered and gone), and path-long (win32 hosts only). Each asserts the code in the log, exactly one report_blocked row (taskId, workerId, reason starting with the code), no CLI run and exit code 1.

Shared-mode cases: shared-unlanded (moe/task/task-postflight holds a commit HEAD lacks) refuses with MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH under the same assertions. shared-landed (the branch at HEAD) launches the CLI with no report_blocked row and no MOE_WORKTREE_ line.

postflight-fake-proxy.js gains only the opt-in knobs FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE, FAKE_CTX_WORKSPACE, FAKE_CTX_COMMITS and report_blocked logging. `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash` and `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` both exit 0.

Red against today's wrappers: the suite exits 1 under bash for sh and under Windows PowerShell 5.1 for ps1. Every case except shared-landed fails on an assertion, not a harness error, and shared-landed passes.

implementationPlan.description:
The suite harness (DoD 1): a new file, scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs, modelled on scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs. Copy its spawn, env and kill shape, but not its stop-at-first-failure loop.

Invocation: `node postflight-worktree.cjs <sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine>`.
- `<this file> cli` is the fake CLI. It appends one line to <MOE_PROJECT_PATH>/.moe/wt-cli.log and exits 0.

Per case:
- a fresh repository under one mkdtemp root, plus a wrapper temp dir this suite deletes;
- MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=<case,...> selects cases;
- MOE_KEEP_WORKTREE_FIXTURE=1 keeps the root;
- cleanup uses rmSync with maxRetries, in finally.

Runner:
- Run every selected case in a try/catch.
- Print `[worktree] <case> ok`, or `[worktree] <case> FAILED: <e.name>: <first line of e.message>`. Step 4 uses that to tell assertions from harness errors.
- Exit 1 if any case failed.
- No line may start with SKIP. On a non-win32 host, path-long prints `[worktree] path-long n/a off win32` and does not count as run.

Fixture (the description's contract):
- `git init`, then `symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main`, core.autocrlf false, and a user name and email.
- Tracked files: .gitignore with `.worktrees/`, src/a.txt, .moe/project.json with {settings:{autoCommit:false}} so a launch lands nothing, and .moe/tasks/task-postflight.json.
- Commit the seed, then `git switch -c moe/control`.
- Untracked runtime: .moe/messages/chan-general.jsonl and .moe/daemon.json, as owner-guard's project() writes them.
- top = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
- A worktree case passes FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE={mode:'worktree', path:top+'/.worktrees/'+task, branch:'moe/task/'+task, target:'main'}.

launch(): owner-guard's argv and env, role worker. inherited drops FAKE_*, WT_* and OG_* keys. It returns {code, log} and does NOT assert exit 0.

Helpers:
- refused(case, code): the log holds `[ERROR] <code>:`. Exactly one evidence-rpcs.jsonl row has tool report_blocked, with args.taskId the task, args.workerId the seat, and args.reason starting with the code. No wt-cli.log exists, and the exit code is 1.
- controlSame(before): the control checkout's HEAD ref and sha, `ls-files -s`, and `status --porcelain=v1 -uall -- . ':(exclude).moe'` are all unchanged.
- wt(dir): parse `worktree list --porcelain -z` into entries: path normalized with forward slashes (case-folded on win32), branch and locked reason.
- The PATH-first git stub:
  - WT_GIT_VERSION answers `git --version` with `git version <v>`.
  - WT_GIT_FAIL=<subcommand> makes that subcommand print to stderr and exit 1. Find the subcommand after any `-C <dir>` and `-c <k=v>` pairs.
  - Everything else execs the real git, at an absolute path resolved once at start.
  - It must work for bash, Git Bash and both PowerShells: an extensionless sh `git` plus a PowerShell-resolvable twin. Verify that PS5.1 picks it before git.exe, and that `'!/.moe/'` survives quoting (mem:gotcha-msys-argv-posix-path-conversion-launcher-tests).

Error handling: every git call in the harness asserts its exit code. A wrapper that outlives MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC is tree-killed and fails its case with a timeout message, never a hang.
implementationPlan.note:
New scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs harness, modelled on postflight-owner-guard.cjs. It takes argv <sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine> and has a `cli` fake-CLI mode that appends cwd to <MOE_PROJECT_PATH>/.moe/wt-cli.log. MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY runs a subset (an unknown name is a FAILED line) and MOE_KEEP_WORKTREE_FIXTURE keeps the fixture. Every case runs in a try/catch and prints `[worktree] <case> ok|FAILED: <e.name>: <first line>`, with the detail indented `  | `, so no line starts with SKIP. path-long prints `n/a off win32` off Windows. Any failure exits 1.
Hermetic env: the inherited filter drops FAKE_/WT_/OG_/MOE_/CLAUDE* (comment-1975f0dd) plus GIT_DIR/WORK_TREE/INDEX_FILE/COMMON_DIR/OBJECT_DIRECTORY, so a hook-run gate can't redirect the fixture's git.
Harness git uses the real git's absolute path. A failed fixture step throws a plain Error, while the wrapper's state is checked through non-throwing probes and asserted, so FAILED lines separate a broken fixture from a wrong wrapper. The log is ANSI-stripped, because sh prints `${RED}[ERROR]${NC}`. A run past MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC is tree-killed and fails its case with a timeout assertion, never a hang.
Git stub: an extensionless sh `git` plus git.ps1. git.ps1 sets EAP=Continue, has no CmdletBinding, forwards $input when ExpectingInput, and exits with $LASTEXITCODE (comment-652631e2).
Fixture deviation: .gitignore also holds `.mcp.json` and `logs/`, as the real repo's does. Every wrapper run writes both into the project whatever the mode (seen: `?? .mcp.json`, `?? logs/moe-usage/<id>.jsonl`), and without the entries controlSame would fail a correct WT-04.
Smoke (HEAD snapshot of scripts/ under /mnt/d/moe-scratch, bash): exit 1, 11 FAILED, all AssertionError, shared-landed ok, 28 s.

implementationPlan.description:
The cases (DoD 2-4), in scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs. Use the task's contract word for word. W = top/.worktrees/task-postflight on moe/task/task-postflight.

lifecycle, one repository and four runs:
1. create: the log says `[worktree] created <W> on moe/task/task-postflight`. Then assert:
   - W is registered and locked with reason `moe task-postflight`;
   - refs/heads/moe/task/task-postflight equals main's tip;
   - W/src/a.txt exists and W/.moe does not;
   - controlSame holds;
   - the CLI ran and the exit code is 0.
2. reuse: write a marker into W's admin dir (`git rev-parse --git-dir` run in W) and a dirty file into W. The run logs `reused`, and the marker and the dirt survive.
3. re-add: commit a change in W onto the task branch, `worktree unlock`, then `worktree remove --force` so the branch stays. The run logs `re-added`. The branch tip is unchanged, W's HEAD equals it, and the committed change is checked out.
4. moe-present: mkdir W/.moe and write W/.moe/x. Then:
   - refused with MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT;
   - W/.moe/x still exists and W is still registered;
   - the task branch has no new commit.

resume: FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=resume and FAKE_TASK_STATUS=WORKING, with the workspace given only through FAKE_CTX_WORKSPACE for task-resume. W is created at .worktrees/task-resume on moe/task/task-resume, and the CLI ran. Write .moe/tasks/task-resume.json if the wrapper reads it.

half-made: pre-create the W with `worktree add --lock --reason "moe task-postflight" --no-checkout --no-track -b moe/task/task-postflight W main` and nothing else, so its index is empty. The run finishes it: W/src/a.txt exists, W/.moe does not, and the CLI ran.

Refusal cases. Each is checked by refused(code), plus the extra assertions listed:
- git-old: WT_GIT_VERSION=2.37.9 gives MOE_WORKTREE_UNSUPPORTED_GIT, and the log names 2.37.9.
- not-top: the project is <repo>/proj, with its .moe there. MOE_WORKTREE_PROJECT_NOT_TOP.
- control: HEAD is left on main. MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING.
- target-missing: workspace target 'nosuch'. MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- mismatch: FAKE_CTX_COMMITS=[{kind:'checkpoint', sha:<a commit only on branch moe/work-2026-10-24>, ref:'moe/work-2026-10-24'}]. MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH.
- dir-exists: an unregistered .worktrees/task-postflight/marker.txt. MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, and the directory and the marker's bytes are untouched.
- sparse-fail: WT_GIT_FAIL=sparse-checkout. MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED; W ends up unregistered and its directory is gone.
- path-long, win32 hosts only:
  - set `core.longpaths false` in the repo;
  - commit a tracked path whose length L makes len(W)+1+L land between 241 and 250, computed from the real W, while len(control)+1+L stays under 259;
  - expect MOE_WORKTREE_PATH_TOO_LONG.
- shared-unlanded: no workspace knob, and refs/heads/moe/task/task-postflight holds a commit HEAD lacks. MOE_WORKTREE_MODE_MISMATCH.

shared-landed: the branch sits at HEAD. The CLI ran, there is no report_blocked row and no `MOE_WORKTREE_` in the log, and the exit code is 0.

Budget: the whole suite file at most 330 lines. The cases must assert git state (refs, the worktree list, file bytes), not only log text.
implementationPlan.note:
13 cases follow the description's contract: lifecycle (create, reuse, re-add, moe-present), resume, half-made, git-old, not-top, control, target-missing, mismatch, dir-exists, sparse-fail, path-long, shared-unlanded and shared-landed. Each asserts git state: the worktree list (path, branch, lock `moe <task>`), task-branch tip and W's HEAD, file bytes, and the control HEAD ref/sha, `ls-files -s -t` and status. Foreign commits are made with commit-tree + update-ref through a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE. The shared-unlanded commit changes the tree. path-long's L is computed from the real W (W+1+L=245, control 218) and committed onto main. half-made expects the verb `reused`, as WT-04's plan says. Suite is 311 lines (budget 330).
Harness fixes found while proving the cases passable:
(a) status excludes `:(exclude,glob)**/.moe/**`, so not-top's proj/.moe is excluded too;
(b) the index check is `ls-files -s -t`, because a sparse-checkout run in the control checkout deletes its tracked .moe and leaves status clean (only the S tag shows it);
(c) Git Bash's bin/bash.exe puts /mingw64/bin ahead of PATH, so sh engines also get BASH_ENV=<stub>/env.sh, which re-prepends the stub (BASH_ENV is also dropped from the inherited env).
GREEN proof: a scratch bash reference implementation of the contract (/mnt/d/moe-scratch/wt04t-ref/ref.sh, not delivered). Linux bash: 12 ok, 0 failed. Win32 Git Bash: 13 ok, 0 failed, path-long included.
Mutants of the reference, each caught: CLI after refusal (9 FAILED), report_blocked twice (9), rm of a pre-existing dir (dir-exists), rm of W/.moe (lifecycle), sparse-checkout in the control checkout (4), re-add with -B (lifecycle: branch tip), ignoring the get_context workspace (resume).
PS5.1 stub probe passed: git.ps1 resolves as ExternalScript ahead of git.exe; `--version` is answered at any position; piped hash-object --stdin-paths works; `--format=%(refname)` survives; exit codes propagate; WT_GIT_FAIL gives rc=1; sparse patterns come through as `/* | !/.moe/`.
For WT-04: under Git Bash, MSYS rewrites the `'/*'` argument of `sparse-checkout set`, and W keeps .moe. The reference needed MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'; the suite catches it via MOE_PRESENT/W/.moe.

Could a correct implementation fail?
- Windows paths: `norm()` applies realpath, `\`→`/`, strips the trailing slash and lowercases on win32, on both the `[worktree]` line and `worktree list -z`. The log is ANSI-stripped.
- Stub quoting:
  - git.ps1 was probed under PS5.1. `%(refname)`, stdin piping, rc propagation and `/* !/.moe/` all survive. It is .ps1 rather than .cmd because cmd mangles `%`.
  - Under Git Bash the stub is re-prepended via BASH_ENV, since bash.exe puts /mingw64/bin first.
  - A correct implementation needs `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` on its sparse call. That is a real WT-04 bug class and was reported in comment-c97655995abd4ff6bab7fb23ee937438.
- Locked W cleanup: `rmSync` with `maxRetries:10`. If that still throws, the run ends red with a stack trace, which is loud, not silent. Noted as theoretical.
- CRLF in wt-cli.log: only the file's presence is checked.
- Timing: `LIMIT=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC||180`s, then killTree plus a timedOut assertion. A hang becomes a failure.
- No `^SKIP` output. path-long prints `n/a off win32`.

Error handling:
- `git()` throws on non-zero.
- `probe()` keeps the exit status in the compared snapshot.
- `revOf()` returns null and is equality-asserted.
- A harness or setup error surfaces as `FAILED: Error:`, which the gate treats as non-AssertionError and fails.

Concurrency: root and wrapperTmp are separate mkdtemp dirs, and cases run sequentially.

Proxy diff:
- With knobs unset it is byte-identical apart from the report_blocked case, which today's wrappers never call (grep confirmed). That case adds an evidence row and returns BLOCKED.
- `jsonKnob` throws on malformed JSON.
- `FAKE_CTX_COMMITS` must be an array.

Rails: tests only, no other file touched, parity-check PASS.

@architect-bd1eb82d I created this row and planned WT-04 (task-c20464ff, rev 1). WT-04's plan follows this description's contract word for word. Pointers from my exploration:

1. Model the suite on scripts/tests/postflight-owner-guard.cjs. Copy its launch()/project() shape and env isolation:

- sh: a bash `git` that answers `--version` with "git version 2.37.9" (or exits 1 when an arg is `sparse-checkout`) and otherwise `exec`s the real git.
- ps1: PowerShell resolves `git` through PATH. A `git.ps1` that forwards `@args` to the real git.exe (path resolved by the suite) avoids cmd.exe's `%` mangling of `--format=%(...)` arguments, which a `.cmd` stub would hit. It must set $ErrorActionPreference='Continue' and `exit $LASTEXITCODE`.

- The admin dir is <gitdir>/worktrees/<basename(W)>. Put the reuse marker there.

4. Fixture tricks:
- Make the foreign commit with commit-tree plus update-ref, so the control checkout stays untouched.
- path-long: `git update-index --add --cacheinfo 100644,<empty blob>,<230-char path>`, then commit and set core.longpaths=false. win32 hosts only; elsewhere print a not-applicable line that does NOT start with SKIP.

- ps1: `node.exe scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs ps1 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(wslpath -w "$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/wt04t.XXXXXX)")" powershell`. node.exe from WSL runs as win32 with the cwd translated.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
Planner note, plan rev 1, from architect-bd1eb82d. The plan was submitted 5 s after comment-fa8bce25 and did not include it. Where the two differ, this note decides. Files, DoD, budgets, argv, case names, codes and knob names are unchanged, so there is no re-plan.

Step 1 (fake proxy):
- FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE also writes workspace=<knob.path> and workspaceMode=<knob.mode> into the attempt record that attemptFixture() writes. This matches ExecutionAttempt's fields in schema.ts. WT-08T asked for it.
- With the knob unset, the record stays byte-identical.
- The wrappers never read attempt.workspace today, so no case changes.

Step 2 (harness):
- inherited also drops MOE_* and CLAUDE* keys, e.g. /^(FAKE_|WT_|OG_|MOE_|CLAUDE)/i. CLAUDECODE has no underscore, hence `CLAUDE` with no trailing underscore.
  - owner-guard's filter keeps MOE_*, so a seat's own MOE_WORKER_ID and session vars leak into the wrapper under test.
  - launch() sets the MOE_* it needs explicitly.
  - The suite must be hermetic: seats run it as their gate.
- The PowerShell stub twin is git.ps1, not git.cmd, because cmd.exe mangles `%` in `--format=%(...)`.
  - It sets $ErrorActionPreference='Continue', forwards @args to the real git.exe at its absolute path, and ends with `exit $LASTEXITCODE`.
  - WT-04's ps1 resolves bare `& git` through PATH, so a PATH-prepended git.ps1 is found first. Still verify that PS5.1 picks it.
- WT_GIT_FAIL, when non-empty, matches any argv element equal to it. That also covers --git-dir/--work-tree forms.
- WT_GIT_VERSION answers `version` as well as `--version`.
- wt(): with -z, each attribute field is NUL-terminated and a record ends with an empty field. The lock field reads `locked moe <task>`.

Step 3 (cases):
- Make foreign commits with commit-tree + update-ref, never by switching the control checkout. This applies to mismatch's moe/work-2026-10-24 commit and to shared-unlanded's task-branch commit.
- shared-unlanded's commit must CHANGE the tree, e.g. add src/b.txt through a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE and write-tree.
  - An empty commit on HEAD^{tree} merges back to HEAD's own tree. The contract counts that as landed, so a correct WT-04 would launch and the case would fail.
- path-long:
  - Keep the computed L (len(W)+1+L in 241..250), not a fixed 230-char path. Only the computed L can tell a 240 threshold from a 260 one.
  - The guard measures the TARGET, so the long path must be in refs/heads/main. Committed on moe/control alone, it would let a correct WT-04 pass the guard and fail the case.
  - The control-side path is 27 chars shorter (214..223), so write the file for real.
  - Assert L > 0.
- The reuse marker stays at `git rev-parse --git-dir` run in W. That is <gitdir>/worktrees/<basename(W)> unless git added a suffix to the name.

Step 4 (verify):
- Keep the HEAD-snapshot runs. Never run the red proof against the shared checkout's live wrappers, as the comment's commands do.
- For the ps1 run, node.exe from WSL over a /mnt/d mktemp is fine.

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
Pointer for this row's worker from WT-04's planner (architect-4ae016fb). It's additive to comment-1975f0dd, which wins where they differ. I tested a git.ps1 stub prepended to PATH under Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe). Five things for the ps1 stub:
1. It resolves as ExternalScript ahead of git.exe, and its `exit N` reaches the caller's $LASTEXITCODE. WT-04 calls git only through PATH: Invoke-MoeGit runs a bare `& git -C $Top @GitArgs` (HEAD:scripts/moe-agent.ps1:2581/2583).
2. Forward piped input. Get-MoeDirtySnapshot (:2697) pipes paths into `& git -C $Top hash-object --stdin-paths`, and the rescue, landing and baseline paths call it (:4227/4708/5194). Inside the stub, ExpectingInput is True and the paths are in $input. Use `if ($MyInvocation.ExpectingInput) { $input | & $real @args } else { & $real @args }`, or the inner git never gets the paths.
3. Answer `--version` at any argv position, the same way WT_GIT_FAIL matches. A probe through Invoke-MoeGit arrives as `-C <Top> --version`. Do the same in the sh stub.
4. The binder swallows a literal `--` in a direct `& git … -- $p` call (:2704). A splatted `--` (Invoke-MoeGit) survives. That's harmless for D:/ paths, but don't assert on it.
5. No [CmdletBinding()] or [Parameter()] in the stub, or `-C` fails to bind. Use plain $args.

It is red against today's wrappers: every case except shared-landed fails on an assertion. The fake proxy gains only opt-in workspace and commit knobs plus report_blocked logging.
acceptanceCriteria: The suite runs with the documented argv, the `cli` mode, MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY and MOE_KEEP_WORKTREE_FIXTURE. It prints one ok or FAILED line per case, never a SKIP line, and exits 1 on any failure.
The lifecycle, resume and half-made cases, the eight guard cases and both shared cases assert the description's contract on git state and on report_blocked rows.
Against HEAD's wrappers the suite exits 1 under bash and under PS5.1. Every FAILED line is an AssertionError, and shared-landed is ok.
